question: Why must the unmanifest be posited as distinct from the modifications of body and senses?
premises: Body and sense organs are effects and modifications.
The unmanifest is considered in relation to these effects.
It is posited as separate from such modifications.
inference: The unmanifest is distinct from the modifications constituting body and senses.
uncertainties: The argument is compressed and may rely on Sāṃkhya-style reasoning.
plain_english: Thus the unmanifest is distinct from the modification that constitutes the effects, namely body and sense organs.
